name: Behind-the-Neck Lat Pulldown
description: The behind-the-neck lat pulldown pulls the bar down behind the head to touch the base of the neck. While it creates a different angle of lat engagement and places greater emphasis on the rear deltoid and rhomboids, this exercise places the shoulder joint in an impingement-prone position and is contraindicated for individuals with shoulder or cervical spine issues. It should only be performed by experienced trainees with demonstrated shoulder mobility.

execution.starting_position: Sit at a lat pulldown machine with a wide-grip bar attachment. Grip the bar with an overhand grip 4-6 inches wider than shoulder width. Lean the torso slightly forward and tuck the chin to the chest.
execution.setup_instructions: Secure thighs under the pads. Set an appropriate weight. Tuck the chin before each repetition.
steps: Step 1: Grip the bar wide with an overhand grip.
Step 2: Tuck the chin firmly to the chest before initiating the movement.
Step 3: Pull the bar downward and behind the head, aiming to touch the base of the neck.
Step 4: Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the bottom position.
Step 5: Return the bar under control to full arm extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Not tucking the chin, risking impact with the cervical vertebrae
Using excessive weight, forcing poor positioning
Pulling too aggressively with shoulder impingement concerns
safety_considerations: Not recommended for individuals with shoulder impingement, rotator cuff issues, or cervical spine problems
Always tuck the chin before each repetition
Many coaches recommend the standard front pulldown as a safer alternative with comparable lat activation
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension at top to bar touching the base of the neck at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Bar to the base of the skull, not lower
Retract shoulder blades at the bottom
